predecessors.name: Visigothic Kingdom
predecessors.text: southern Baetica from Málaga to the mouth of the Guadalete (Medina Sidonia included), with the Algarve

successors.name: Visigothic Kingdom
successors.text: 'What Sisebut had begun by retaking Cartagena, Malaga, Sagunto, and Assidonia from the Byzantines, Suintila finished in 624' (Suintila page)

ledger.x: 552: Justinian's army lands in southern Spain.
Early March 555: a Byzantine force from Italy lands at Cartagena.
By 619: Málaga and Cartagena are Visigothic.
By 619: the fighting for Málaga and Cartagena ends.
624: Suintila takes the last Byzantine land.

wars.name: Byzantine intervention in the Visigothic civil war
wars.outcome: Athanagild's revolt against Agila I (550-551) led him to ask Justinian for help; the Byzantine army landed in 552 and defeated Agila; a force from Italy landed at Cartagena in March 555; Agila was killed in late March and Athanagild became king, the…

wars.name: Visigothic reconquest of Spania
wars.outcome: Leovigild retook Medina Sidonia in 572 and put down Córdoba's rebellion; Sisebut made two expeditions in 614-615 and had Málaga before 619; Suintila 'finished' the reconquest in 624 with the Algarve.

certainty.note: The province was a coastal strip that 'never extended very far inland'; no page gives a line.
